text:
Sam: Heads up — new reranker int8 bring-up showing a weird MRR drop on our holdout, looks like -7% relative to float. NDCG slightly up so this smells like a formatting/change-in-order issue.
Priya: raw numbers?
Sam: quick summary: NDCG@10 +0.3%, MRR@10 -7.2% (holdout run). eval harness id: run/2026-03-20/56
Jordan: hmm. did we change serializer or any unicode normalisation for the candidate text when creating the candidate pool?
Sam: found noise in a tiny sample — trailing non-breaking spaces and mixed unicode dashes. Example snippet:
```
query: "how to reset pwd"
candidate: "Reset password · guide\u00A0\n"
```
Sam: tokenizer splits \u00A0 differently, and under quantized kernels scoring shifts for those tokens.
Priya: right — small token differences can change softmax ordering which hits MRR more than NDCG.
Luca: also double-check PTQ config. What was used for this build? batch size, per-channel, seed?
Sam: PTQ config pasted from job: `quant_mode=int8_dynamic, per_channel=false, calibr_samples=2048, batch_size=64, seed=42`
Priya: try per_channel=true and bump calibr_samples. also run with and without the unicode normaliser (NFKC) to isolate.
Jordan: I can run a shadowbench with a focused 10k query holdout if you push a dataset diff.
Sam: pushed dataset diff and small repro script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/789
eval-bot: shadowbench started: sb-789 — est duration 2h — logs -> /ops/logs/sb-789
Priya: quick local probe on 1k examples: before patch MRR=0.421, after stripping trailing whitespace MRR=0.450. So this is highly localised to whitespace/token differences.
Sam: plan: 1) add NFKC normalisation to serializer, 2) re-run PTQ with `per_channel=true, calibr_samples=8192`, 3) shadowbench A/B on 10k holdout, 4) if still bad, revert quant and dig into kernel selection differences.
Jordan: assigning: @Sam -> repro + push small filter, @Priya -> calibration sweep and short ablation, @Luca -> monitor shadowbench ops and collect traces
Sam: noted, starting runs now :thumbsup:
eval-bot: sb-789 finished: baseline vs patched serializer: NDCG@10 +0.2%, MRR@10 +1.1% (patched wins)
Priya: looks like the normaliser fixed the systematic tokenisation issue. We should add a unit test for trailing NBSP/zero-width spaces into the preproc CI.
Sam: created PR #792 that adds NFKC normalization + unit tests and a small regen step for bench data.
Jordan: awesome, merge after perf sign-off. any followups?
Luca: we should also add a tiny synthetic test to the rerank smoke that injects weird whitespace and asserts no MRR regression >1%.
Sam: will add that to the CI checklist. closing loop unless anything else pops up. Thanks everyone.
